# Multi-KB Workflow — verify two knowledge bases stay isolated. Every
# invocation addresses exactly one base, with --kb or AKB_KB.

exec akb init kb-a
stdout 'Initialized KB .kb-a.'

exec akb init kb-b
stdout 'Initialized KB .kb-b.'

# Write to KB-A only.
stdin note-a.md
exec akb --kb kb-a write note-a.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/note-a.md'

# KB-A shows its page and none of KB-B's work.
exec akb --kb kb-a list
stdout 'notes/note-a.md'
! stdout 'note-b'

exec akb --kb kb-a search 'knowledge base A'
stdout 'notes/note-a.md'
! stdout 'note-b'

# Write to KB-B only.
stdin note-b.md
exec akb --kb kb-b write note-b.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/note-b.md'

exec akb --kb kb-b list
stdout 'notes/note-b.md'
! stdout 'note-a'

exec akb --kb kb-b search 'knowledge base B'
stdout 'notes/note-b.md'
! stdout 'note-a'

# KB-A is unchanged by the work in KB-B.
exec akb --kb kb-a list
stdout 'notes/note-a.md'
! stdout 'note-b'

# An environment selection addresses the same base as the flag.
env AKB_KB=kb-a
exec akb list
stdout 'notes/note-a.md'
! stdout 'note-b'

-- note-a.md --
---
type: note
title: Note in KB A
summary: Page for KB A
tags: multikb
---
Content for knowledge base A.

-- note-b.md --
---
type: note
title: Note in KB B
summary: Page for KB B
tags: multikb
---
Content for knowledge base B.
